Statement of Support for Mayor Joy Belmonte’s Call for Coordination and Transparency in Flood Control Projects

As a citizen and advocate for health, governance, and systemic reform, I stand in full support of Mayor Joy Belmonte’s principled stance regarding the P14-billion flood control projects in Quezon City that were implemented without proper coordination with the local government unit (LGU) 

Under the Local Government Code, LGUs are not mere spectators—they are the frontline stewards of their communities. 

The absence of coordination in 252 out of 254 flood control projects undermines not only the spirit of decentralization but also the safety and welfare of the people of Quezon City.

Flooding in key areas such as Commonwealth Avenue and surrounding districts is no longer a seasonal inconvenience—it is a public health hazard, an infrastructure crisis, and a test of leadership. 

Mayor Belmonte’s call for transparency and collaborative planning is not just timely—it is essential.

We urge national agencies, particularly the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), to uphold the principles of good governance by ensuring that all future projects are aligned with local priorities, vetted through proper channels, and executed with full accountability.

In times of crisis, coordinated leadership is not optional—it is the only path forward. Mayor Belmonte’s resolve reflects the kind of moral courage and administrative clarity that our cities need to thrive.

Let this be a turning point—not just for Quezon City, but for all LGUs seeking to reclaim their rightful role in shaping resilient, responsive communities.

Dr. Tony Leachon 

#KleptopirosisIsReal 
#RelentlessForChange

Exercise ALON 2025 Closes with Stronger Partnerships, Shared Resolve for Peace

The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and the Australian Defence Force (ADF) formally concluded Exercise ALON 2025 during a Closing Ceremony today, August 29, held at Tejeros Hall, AFP Commissioned Officers’ Country, here.

The event was graced by Major General Paul Kenny DSC, AM, DSM, Deputy Theater Commander–Australia; Major General Francisco F Lorenzo Jr PA, AFP Exercise Director, ALON 25; Lieutenant General Jimmy D Larida PN(M), Acting Chief of Staff, AFP, who represented General Romeo S Brawner Jr, AFP Chief of Staff; His Excellency Marc Innes-Brown PSM, Australian Ambassador to the Philippines; and Senior Undersecretary Irineo C Espino, Undersecretary of National Defense (USND), who represented Secretary of National Defense Gilberto C Teodoro Jr.

Running from August 15 to 29, Exercise ALON 2025 was conducted across multiple locations in Palawan, Nueva Ecija, and within the waters of West Philippine Sea. Major activities included amphibious operations, naval and air interoperability drills, maritime security operations, and combined live-fire exercises. Beyond combat training, the exercise also featured humanitarian and disaster response activities, community relations projects, and cultural exchanges, highlighting the holistic approach of AFP and ADF in fostering cooperation.

In his message, LtGen Larida underscored the significance of the exercise: “In these uncertain times when challenges on sovereignty, freedom of navigation, and the rule of law persist, our collaboration sends a clear message: that nations, large and small, have stood together, side by side in the defense of peace and rights of all people.”///

Photos by: A1C Castro PAF / PAOAFP

#AFPyoucanTRUST
#OneAFPOnePHILIPPINES
#StrongAFPStrongPHILIPPINES
#OurSeasOurRightsOurFuture

data.raw_text:
Traffic Advisory 

This morning, Police registered a fatal accident at Seeta involving a concrete mixer and a truck, which unfortunately claimed one life. Efforts are currently underway to have the vehicles towed away in order to restore smooth traffic flow.
In the meantime, we appeal to all motorists to use the following alternative routes to avoid traffic congestion in the affected area:
• Motorists from the City Centre heading to Kireka are advised to use the Kinawataka – Kirinya – Jokas route.
• Motorists using the Northern Bypass are advised to branch off at Naalya Roundabout – Kyaliwajala – Sonde – Seeta.
• Motorists from Mukono heading to the City Centre are advised to use Kalagi Road.
We regret the loss of life and extend our condolences to the family of the deceased. Further details will be communicated in due course.
We apologize for the inconvenience caused and thank the public for their cooperation.
